title: How Adam Robinson scaled Retention.com to $22M with six people and launched RB2B on LinkedIn
summary: Adam Robinson walks through Retention.com's P&L (about 87% gross margin, roughly $6M net income run rate), his failed 2023 push to scale like a funded rival, and how a candid LinkedIn post about a vendor's cease and desist gave RB2B 1,600 pre-launch leads. He also discusses RB2B's credit-based pricing, high free-to-paid conversion, and his open concerns about churn.

principles.text: A data business can hold high margins at scale by turning data costs into a fixed cost.
principles.quote: you compile a lot of data at SAS margins and then you don't really have to increase the spend on that data if you do it the right way and you kind of make the cost fixed

principles.text: Funded peers and vanity metrics tempt bootstrappers into overspending; staying disciplined is hard on the ego.
principles.quote: it just takes a lot for your ego to withstand everything that's trying to make you a bigger vanity metric company

principles.text: Honest, unpolished founder storytelling beats PR-filtered brand content for building resonance.
principles.quote: you end up with fluffy crap at the end that no one can resonate with

principles.text: Organic social works when it is mostly value and story, with only the occasional hard CTA.
principles.quote: hardly any of it is sales content you know maybe one out of every 10 post I'll put some like hard CTA at the bottom of it

principles.text: Run heavy customer discovery calls before launch so you know what to build.
principles.quote: SOS and I were getting on the phone with like 10 people a day between the two of us for like six months so we really had a good idea of what we wanted to deliver at launch

principles.text: Content aimed at a tight audience drives unusually strong activation and free-to-paid conversion.
principles.quote: the content is targeting such a tight audience of the right people on LinkedIn and it's just leading to that
